problem_summary.summary: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the current minimum, with every operation taking constant time.
problem_summary.input_output: Implement MinStack with its constructor, push(int), pop(), top(), and getMin() methods.
constraints: pop, top, and getMin are called only when nonempty

brute_force.explanation: Store values in an array-backed list. Push, pop, and top use the end of the list; getMin scans all current values.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The list contains exactly the stack contents in bottom-to-top order. Its final value is the top, and scanning all entries computes the minimum currently present.
brute_force.time_complexity: push, pop, and top are O(1) amortized; getMin is O(n) for a stack of n values.

optimized.explanation: Maintain a value stack and a parallel minimum stack. Push the new value onto the minimum stack when it is no greater than the current minimum; pop both stacks together when removing a value.
optimized.correctness_idea: The minimum stack records the minimum for each depth at which that minimum becomes active. Equal minima are recorded too, so popping one duplicate cannot erase the minimum while another copy remains.
optimized.time_complexity: O(1) for push, pop, top, and getMin.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for values and up to O(n) additional entries in the minimum stack.

steps.action: Push each value and record each equal minimum.
Pop both; the remaining -1 still represents the minimum, and top() returns -1.

edge_cases.handling: The optimized minimum stack records equal values and removes one copy per matching pop.
The previous minimum is exposed by the parallel stack.
Comparisons use integer ordering without arithmetic transformations.
